sentences.text: Bactrosaurus was a herbivorous hadrosauroid dinosaur that lived in Asia between 96 and 85 million years ago.
A typical individual measured between 6 and 6.5 meters in length and weighed approximately 1.2 metric tons, though other estimates place the weight between 1,100 and 1,500 kilograms.
The femur of this animal measured 80 centimeters in length.
Large vertebral spines on its back may have supported a hump.
Like other hadrosaurs, it could adapt to both bipedal and quadrupedal postures.
A subsequent study revealed fragments that appear to be the base of an incompletely preserved crest on Bactrosaurus.
Recent studies suggest Bactrosaurus was likely crestless because basal hadrosauromorphs do not preserve hollow crests.
The first remains were partial skeletons of six individuals found in the Iren Dabasu Formation of the Gobi Desert, China.
Charles W. Gilmore described and named the species in 1933, referencing the large club-shaped neural spines on its vertebrae.
A 2026 study of fossils collected in 2014 and 2015 suggests Bactrosaurus johnsoni exhibited herding behavior and population segregation between juveniles and adults.
While over 10,000 fossils were examined for tumors, the specific types found in Bactrosaurus were limited to this genus and closely related genera.
Researchers suggest the tumors found in Bactrosaurus may have been caused by either environmental factors or genetic propensity.
Bactrosaurus is classified within the suborder Iguanodontia and the superfamily Hadrosauroidea.
The time range for Bactrosaurus is recorded as extending from the Turonian to the Campanian stages, between 93.9 and 72.2 million years ago.
